title: Traveling Salesman Tour
description:
A courier must start at city 1, visit every one of the n cities exactly once, and finally return to city 1. Travelling directly from city i to city j costs d[i][j]. Costs are not necessarily symmetric (d[i][j] may differ from d[j][i]). Find the minimum total cost of such a tour.

With n = 1 the courier never moves and the cost is 0.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 14
  • 0 ≤ d[i][j] ≤ 106, d[i][i] = 0
  • Trying all (n−1)! orders is far too slow for n = 14.

Input

  • Line 1: integer n.
  • Next n lines: n integers each; the j-th number on line i is d[i][j].

Output

A single integer: the minimum tour cost.

Example

Input:

4
0 10 15 20
10 0 35 25
15 35 0 30
20 25 30 0

Output:

80
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    d = [[int(t[1 + i * n + j]) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
    if n == 1:
        print(0)
        return
    INF = 1 << 60
    full = (1 << n) - 1
    dp = [[INF] * n for _ in range(1 << n)]
    dp[1][0] = 0
    for mask in range(1, 1 << n, 2):
        row = dp[mask]
        outs = [b for b in range(1, n) if not (mask >> b) & 1]
        if not outs:
            continue
        for last in range(n):
            c = row[last]
            if c >= INF:
                continue
            dl = d[last]
            for nx in outs:
                v = c + dl[nx]
                tgt = dp[mask | (1 << nx)]
                if v < tgt[nx]:
                    tgt[nx] = v
    print(min(dp[full][j] + d[j][0] for j in range(1, n)))
main()

title: Workers and Jobs Assignment
description:
There are n workers and n jobs. Worker i can do job j for cost c[i][j], or cannot do it at all when c[i][j] = −1. Assign every worker to a different job so that every job is done and the total cost is minimum.

If no complete assignment exists, print -1.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 15
  • c[i][j] = −1 or 0 ≤ c[i][j] ≤ 106
  • Greedy choices fail; trying all n! assignments is too slow.

Input

  • Line 1: integer n.
  • Next n lines: n integers; line i holds c[i][1] … c[i][n].

Output

A single integer: the minimum total cost, or -1.

Example

Input:

3
9 2 7
6 4 3
5 8 1

Output:

9
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    c = [[int(t[1 + i * n + j]) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
    INF = 1 << 60
    size = 1 << n
    dp = [INF] * size
    dp[0] = 0
    for mask in range(size):
        v = dp[mask]
        if v >= INF:
            continue
        i = bin(mask).count("1")
        if i == n:
            continue
        row = c[i]
        for j in range(n):
            w = row[j]
            if w >= 0 and not (mask >> j) & 1:
                nm = mask | (1 << j)
                if v + w < dp[nm]:
                    dp[nm] = v + w
    print(dp[size - 1] if dp[size - 1] < INF else -1)
main()

title: Burst Balloons for Coins
description:
n balloons stand in a row; balloon i shows number a[i]. You burst them one at a time, in any order you like. Bursting balloon i earns left · a[i] · right coins, where left and right are the numbers on the balloons that are currently its nearest remaining neighbours (a missing neighbour counts as 1). After bursting, the neighbours become adjacent.

Find the maximum number of coins you can collect by bursting all balloons.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 200
  • 0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 100
  • Trying all n! orders is impossible; think about which balloon is burst last in an interval.

Input

  • Line 1: integer n.
  • Line 2: n integers a[1] … a[n].

Output

A single integer: the maximum coins.

Example

Input:

4
3 1 5 8

Output:

167
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    b = [1] + [int(x) for x in t[1:1 + n]] + [1]
    m = n + 2
    dp = [[0] * m for _ in range(m)]   # dp[i][j]: best for open interval (i, j)
    col = [[0] * m for _ in range(m)]  # col[j][k] = dp[k][j]
    for length in range(2, m):
        for i in range(0, m - length):
            j = i + length
            bij = b[i] * b[j]
            di = dp[i]
            cj = col[j]
            best = 0
            for k in range(i + 1, j):
                v = di[k] + cj[k] + bij * b[k]
                if v > best:
                    best = v
            di[j] = best
            cj[i] = best
    print(dp[0][m - 1])
main()

title: Best and Worst Meeting Point
description:
A country has n towns connected by n − 1 two-way roads so that every town can reach every other (a tree). Road i has length w.

For a town v, let S(v) be the sum of shortest-path distances from v to all towns. Find the town with the smallest S and the town with the largest S. If several towns tie, choose the one with the smallest index.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ w ≤ 104
  • Running a search from every town is O(n²) — too slow. The tree can be a long path, so avoid deep recursion.

Input

  • Line 1: integer n.
  • Next n − 1 lines: u v w — a road between towns u and v of length w.

Output

  • Line 1: S_min v_min
  • Line 2: S_max v_max

Example

Input:

4
1 2 1
2 3 1
2 4 1

Output:

3 2
5 1
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n - 1):
        u = int(t[1 + 3 * i]); v = int(t[2 + 3 * i]); w = int(t[3 + 3 * i])
        adj[u].append((v, w)); adj[v].append((u, w))
    parent = [0] * (n + 1)
    pw = [0] * (n + 1)
    order = [1]
    parent[1] = -1
    for x in order:
        for y, w in adj[x]:
            if y != parent[x]:
                parent[y] = x; pw[y] = w; order.append(y)
    size = [1] * (n + 1)
    total = 0
    for x in reversed(order):
        if x != 1:
            size[parent[x]] += size[x]
            total += size[x] * pw[x]
    S = [0] * (n + 1)
    S[1] = total
    for x in order:
        if x != 1:
            S[x] = S[parent[x]] + pw[x] * (n - 2 * size[x])
    vals = S[1:]
    mn = min(vals); mx = max(vals)
    print(mn, vals.index(mn) + 1)
    print(mx, vals.index(mx) + 1)
main()

title: Counting Increasing Subsequences
description:
Given an array a of n integers, count its strictly increasing subsequences of length at least 1. A subsequence is chosen by a set of indices i1 < i2 < … < ik; two subsequences are different if their index sets differ, even if the values are the same. It is strictly increasing if a[i1] < a[i2] < … < a[ik].

Print the count modulo 109 + 7.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·104
  • −109 ≤ a[i] ≤ 109
  • An O(n²) DP is too slow; you need O(n log n).

Input

  • Line 1: integer n.
  • Line 2: n integers.

Output

A single integer: the count modulo 109+7.

Example

Input:

3
1 2 3

Output:

7
solution:
import sys
def main():
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    t = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    a = [int(x) for x in t[1:1 + n]]
    rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted(set(a)))}
    m = len(rank)
    tree = [0] * (m + 1)
    total = 0
    for x in a:
        r = rank[x] - 1
        s = 1
        while r > 0:
            s += tree[r]
            r &= r - 1
        s %= MOD
        total += s
        r = rank[x]
        while r <= m:
            tree[r] = (tree[r] + s) % MOD
            r += r & -r
    print(total % MOD)
main()

title: Disjoint Bitmask Pairs
description:
You are given n integers, each below 216. Count the pairs of positions (i, j) with i < j such that a[i] AND a[j] = 0 (bitwise AND, i.e. the two numbers share no set bit).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 0 ≤ a[i] < 65536
  • Checking every pair is about 5·109 operations; even grouping equal values leaves too many pairs of distinct values. Think sum over subsets.

Input

  • Line 1: integer n.
  • Line 2: n integers.

Output

A single integer: the number of pairs (exact, no modulo).

Example

Input:

4
1 2 3 4

Output:

4
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(t[0])
    a = [int(x) for x in t[1:1 + n]]
    B = 16
    size = 1 << B
    f = [0] * size
    for x in a:
        f[x] += 1
    # f[mask] = how many a[i] are submasks of mask
    for b in range(B):
        bit = 1 << b
        step = bit << 1
        for base in range(0, size, step):
            hi = base + bit
            f[hi:hi + bit] = [x + y for x, y in zip(f[hi:hi + bit], f[base:hi])]
    full = size - 1
    total = 0
    for x in a:
        total += f[full ^ x]
    zeros = f[0]
    print((total - zeros) // 2)
main()

title: Domino Tiling with Holes
description:
A floor is an r × c grid. Some cells are broken (#) and must stay uncovered; all other cells (.) must be covered. Count the ways to cover every free cell with 1 × 2 dominoes (horizontal or vertical) so that dominoes do not overlap and never cover a broken cell.

If every cell is broken, there is exactly 1 way (place nothing). Print the count modulo 109 + 7.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ r ≤ 8
  • 1 ≤ c ≤ 200
  • Use a DP over the boundary profile (broken-profile DP).

Input

  • Line 1: integers r and c.
  • Next r lines: strings of length c made of . and #.

Output

A single integer: the number of tilings modulo 109+7.

Example

Input:

2 3
...
...

Output:

3
solution:
import sys
def main():
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    r, c = int(t[0]), int(t[1])
    g = t[2:2 + r]
    size = 1 << r
    dp = [0] * size
    dp[0] = 1
    for j in range(c):
        for i in range(r):
            new = [0] * size
            free = g[i][j] == '.'
            right = j + 1 < c and g[i][j + 1] == '.'
            down = i + 1 < r and g[i + 1][j] == '.'
            bi = 1 << i
            bd = 1 << (i + 1)
            for mask in range(size):
                v = dp[mask]
                if not v:
                    continue
                if mask & bi:
                    m2 = mask ^ bi
                    new[m2] = (new[m2] + v) % MOD
                elif not free:
                    new[mask] = (new[mask] + v) % MOD
                else:
                    if right:
                        m2 = mask | bi
                        new[m2] = (new[m2] + v) % MOD
                    if down and not (mask & bd):
                        m2 = mask | bd
                        new[m2] = (new[m2] + v) % MOD
            dp = new
    print(dp[0] % MOD)
main()

title: Heavy Knapsack, Light Values
description:
There are n items; item i has weight w[i] and value v[i]. Choose a subset with total weight at most W and maximum total value. Each item can be taken at most once.

Here the weights and the capacity are huge, so the usual table indexed by capacity does not fit — but the values are small.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 100
  • 1 ≤ W ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ w[i] ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ v[i] ≤ 100

Input

  • Line 1: integers n and W.
  • Next n lines: w[i] v[i].

Output

A single integer: the maximum total value.

Example

Input:

3 8
3 30
4 50
5 60

Output:

90
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, W = int(t[0]), int(t[1])
    items = [(int(t[2 + 2 * i]), int(t[3 + 2 * i])) for i in range(n)]
    V = sum(v for _, v in items)
    INF = 1 << 62
    dp = [INF] * (V + 1)   # dp[val] = minimum weight reaching exactly value val
    dp[0] = 0
    top = 0
    for w, v in items:
        top += v
        for val in range(top, v - 1, -1):
            cand = dp[val - v] + w
            if cand < dp[val]:
                dp[val] = cand
    best = 0
    for val in range(V, -1, -1):
        if dp[val] <= W:
            best = val
            break
    print(best)
main()

title: Subset Sums in a Range
description:
Given n integers (possibly negative), count the subsets whose sum s satisfies L ≤ s ≤ R. The empty subset (sum 0) counts too. Subsets are chosen by positions, so equal values at different positions give different subsets.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 36
  • |a[i]| ≤ 1012
  • −4·1013 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 4·1013
  • 236 subsets is too many, and the sums are too large for a DP table. Split the array in half.

Input

  • Line 1: integers n L R.
  • Line 2: n integers.

Output

A single integer: the number of subsets.

Example

Input:

3 2 4
1 2 3

Output:

4
solution:
import sys
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n, L, R = int(t[0]), int(t[1]), int(t[2])
    a = [int(x) for x in t[3:3 + n]]
    def sums(arr):
        s = [0]
        for x in arr:
            s += [y + x for y in s]
        return s
    left = sums(a[:n // 2])
    right = sums(a[n // 2:])
    right.sort()
    cnt = 0
    for x in left:
        cnt += bisect_right(right, R - x) - bisect_left(right, L - x)
    print(cnt)
main()

title: Board Game with Trapdoors
description:
A token starts on square 0 of a board with squares 0, 1, …, N. Each turn you roll a fair die with faces 1 … m and move forward that many squares, except that if the move would go past square N, the token does not move (the turn is still used). Some squares are trapdoors: landing on one immediately sends the token back to square 0 (in the same turn). The game ends when the token lands exactly on square N.

The expected number of turns is a rational number p / q. Print p · q−1 mod (109 + 7). It is guaranteed that the answer is finite and that q is not divisible by 109+7.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 2·105
  • 1 ≤ m ≤ 2·105
  • Trapdoors are distinct squares in 1 … N−1; there are never m or more consecutive trapdoors.
  • Hint: the trapdoors make every expectation depend on the unknown E[0] itself — write each E[i] as A[i] + B[i]·E[0].

Input

  • Line 1: integers N m T (T = number of trapdoors).
  • Line 2: T integers, the trapdoor squares (the line is empty when T = 0).

Output

A single integer: the expected number of turns modulo 109+7.

Example

Input:

2 2 0

Output:

2
solution:
import sys
def main():
    MOD = 10 ** 9 + 7
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    N, m, T = int(t[0]), int(t[1]), int(t[2])
    trap = bytearray(N + 1)
    for x in t[3:3 + T]:
        trap[int(x)] = 1
    lim = min(m, N)
    inv = [0, 1] + [0] * lim
    for i in range(2, lim + 1):
        inv[i] = (MOD - (MOD // i) * inv[MOD % i] % MOD) % MOD
    A = [0] * (N + 2)
    B = [0] * (N + 2)
    SA = [0] * (N + 2)  # suffix sums: SA[i] = A[i] + ... + A[N]
    SB = [0] * (N + 2)
    for i in range(N - 1, -1, -1):
        if trap[i] and i > 0:
            A[i], B[i] = 0, 1
        else:
            cnt = min(m, N - i)
            sa = (SA[i + 1] - SA[i + 1 + cnt]) % MOD
            sb = (SB[i + 1] - SB[i + 1 + cnt]) % MOD
            iv = inv[cnt]
            A[i] = (m + sa) * iv % MOD
            B[i] = sb * iv % MOD
        SA[i] = (SA[i + 1] + A[i]) % MOD
        SB[i] = (SB[i + 1] + B[i]) % MOD
    print(A[0] * pow((1 - B[0]) % MOD, MOD - 2, MOD) % MOD)
main()

title: Frog on Rising Stones
description:
There are n stones with strictly increasing heights h[1] < h[2] < … < h[n]. A frog starts on stone 1 and wants to reach stone n. From stone i it may jump to any stone j > i, paying (h[j] − h[i])² + C.

Find the minimum total cost to reach stone n (0 if n = 1).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105
  • 1 ≤ h[i] ≤ 106, strictly increasing
  • 0 ≤ C ≤ 1012
  • The obvious DP is O(n²). Each candidate is a line in h[j] — use the convex hull trick.

Input

  • Line 1: integers n and C.
  • Line 2: n integers h[1] … h[n].

Output

A single integer: the minimum cost.

Example

Input:

5 6
1 2 3 4 5

Output:

20
solution:
import sys
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, C = int(t[0]), int(t[1])
    h = [int(x) for x in t[2:2 + n]]
    # dp[i] = h_i^2 + C + min_j (-2 h_j * h_i + dp[j] + h_j^2)
    M = [0] * n  # slopes (decreasing)
    K = [0] * n  # intercepts
    head = 0
    tail = 0
    M[0] = -2 * h[0]
    K[0] = h[0] * h[0]
    tail = 1
    dpi = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        x = h[i]
        while tail - head >= 2 and M[head + 1] * x + K[head + 1] <= M[head] * x + K[head]:
            head += 1
        dpi = M[head] * x + K[head] + x * x + C
        m3 = -2 * x
        k3 = dpi + x * x
        while tail - head >= 2:
            m1, k1 = M[tail - 2], K[tail - 2]
            m2, k2 = M[tail - 1], K[tail - 1]
            # line2 is useless if intersection(1,3) <= intersection(1,2)
            if (k3 - k1) * (m1 - m2) <= (k2 - k1) * (m1 - m3):
                tail -= 1
            else:
                break
        M[tail] = m3
        K[tail] = k3
        tail += 1
    print(dpi if n > 1 else 0)
main()

title: Cut the Sequence
description:
Split an array of n non-negative integers into consecutive non-empty segments so that the sum of every segment is at most S. The cost of a split is the sum, over all segments, of the maximum element of the segment. Find the minimum possible cost, or print -1 if no valid split exists.

For S = 17 and 2 2 2 8 1 8 2 1 the best split is [2 2 2] [8 1 8] [2 1] with cost 2 + 8 + 2 = 12 (the middle segment's sum is exactly 17, which is allowed).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 105
  • 0 ≤ a[i] ≤ 106
  • 0 ≤ S ≤ 1012
  • O(n²) is too slow. Combine a monotonic deque of segment maxima with a heap (or another ordered structure).

Input

  • Line 1: integers n and S.
  • Line 2: n integers.

Output

A single integer: the minimum cost, or -1.

Example

Input:

8 17
2 2 2 8 1 8 2 1

Output:

12
solution:
import sys, heapq
from collections import deque
def main():
    t = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, S = int(t[0]), int(t[1])
    a = [0] + [int(x) for x in t[2:2 + n]]
    if max(a[1:]) > S:
        print(-1)
        return
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        P[i] = P[i - 1] + a[i]
    dp = [0] * (n + 1)
    alive = bytearray(n + 1)
    q = deque()
    heap = []
    lo = 0
    push, pop = heapq.heappush, heapq.heappop
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        ai = a[i]
        while P[i] - P[lo] > S:
            lo += 1
        while q and a[q[-1]] <= ai:
            alive[q.pop()] = 0
        if q:
            push(heap, (dp[q[-1]] + ai, q[-1], i))
        q.append(i)
        alive[i] = 1
        while q[0] <= lo:
            alive[q.popleft()] = 0
        best = dp[lo] + a[q[0]]
        while heap and not (alive[heap[0][1]] and alive[heap[0][2]]):
            pop(heap)
        if heap and heap[0][0] < best:
            best = heap[0][0]
        dp[i] = best
    print(dp[n])
main()
